extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent prosecutors, and patent applicants / practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for the form, wording, dependency, fee treatment, and support of patent claims (including multiple dependent claims), directed to examiners and practitioners handling U.S. patent applications under MPEP and CFR rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate correction required for informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this form paragraph to point out minor informalities such as spelling errors, inconsistent terminology, etc., which should be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the informalities render the claim(s) indefinite, use form paragraph 7.34.01 instead to reject the claim(s) under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters must be enclosed within parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims are objected to because they include reference characters which are not enclosed within parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters corresponding to elements recited in the detailed description of the drawings and used in conjunction with the recitation of the same element or group of elements in the claims should be enclosed within parentheses so as to avoid confusion with other numbers or characters which may appear in the claims. See MPEP § 608.01(m). Use of this paragraph is optional; alternatively correct at allowance by informal examiner's amendment. If lack of parentheses renders the claim(s) indefinite, use form paragraph 7.34.01 to reject under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing of lines in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims are objected to because the lines are crowded too closely together, making reading difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute claims with lines one and one-half or double spaced on good quality paper are required. See 37 CFR 1.52(b). Amendments to the claims must be in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependent claim form (alternative only)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple dependent claim shall refer to such other claims in the alternative only. A multiple dependent claim shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fee calculation purposes a multiple dependent claim will be considered to be that number of claims to which direct reference is made therein. Claims in dependent form shall be construed to include all the limitations of the claim incorporated by reference. 35 U.S.C. 112 authorizes multiple dependent claims in applications filed on and after January 24, 1978, as long as they are in alternative form. Cumulative claiming (e.g., 'claims 3 and 4') is not permitted. A multiple dependent claim may refer in the alternative to only one set of claims and may not serve as a basis for another multiple dependent claim either directly or indirectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable and unacceptable multiple dependent claim wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of acceptable multiple dependent claim wording (e.g., 'A gadget according to claims 3 or 4...') and unacceptable wording (e.g., cumulative 'claim 3 and 4', references to non-alternative sets, references to two sets of claims for different features, references to another multiple dependent claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided acceptable examples as templates. Unacceptable forms include 'claim 3 and 4' (conjunctive), referring to numerically succeeding claims in a way that cannot be understood, referencing two sets of claims to different features, or depending from another multiple dependent claim. Such defects should be objected to or handled per form paragraph 7.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper multiple dependent claims objection (form paragraph 7.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to under 37 CFR 1.75(c) as being in improper form because a multiple dependent claim [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2, insert '--should refer to other claims in the alternative only--' and/or '--cannot depend from any other multiple dependent claim--'. Use this paragraph rather than 35 U.S.C. 112, fifth paragraph. In bracket 3, insert '--has--' or '--s have--'. Examples illustrate when to object. Examiner note guidance provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice for multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For restriction purposes, each embodiment of a multiple dependent claim is considered in the same manner as a single dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction may be required between the embodiments of a multiple dependent claim. Some embodiments may be held withdrawn while others are considered on the merits. A multiple dependent claim must be considered as a plurality of single dependent claims for restriction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP handling of multiple dependent claims and fee verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) is responsible for verifying whether multiple dependent claims filed with the application are in proper alternative form, that they depend only upon prior independent or single dependent claims and also for calculating the amount of the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/07 is designed for fee calculation and is used with PTO/SB/06. OPAP places the form in the file where multiple dependent claims are present as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: TC technical support staff handling of added multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Technology Center technical support staff is responsible for verifying compliance with the statute and rules of multiple dependent claims added by amendment and for calculating the amount of any additional fees required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter an amendment containing a new multiple dependent claim or changing dependency before checking whether paid fees cover the amended claims. Contact applicant/attorney to pay additional fees; include a copy of PTO/SB/07 when informing applicant in an insufficient fee situation. Note: OPAP already verifies initial filing fee accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure for claims referring to numerically succeeding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If any series of dependent claims contains a claim with an improper reference to a numerically following claim which cannot be understood, the claim referring to a following claim should normally be objected to and not treated on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, where a claim refers to a numerically following claim and the dependency is clear both as presented and as it will be renumbered at issue, all claims should be examined on the merits and no objection as to form need be made; examiner will renumber at allowance. Bring unusual problems to supervisor's attention. Examples (A and B) illustrate acceptable handling and renumbering practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification practice when referring to dependent claim embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) When identifying a singular dependent claim which does not include a reference to a multiple dependent claim, reference should be made only to the number of the dependent claim. (B) When identifying the embodiments included within a multiple dependent claim... use the number of the claims involved, starting with the highest, to the extent necessary. (C) When all embodiments are subject to a common rejection, reference may be made only to the number of the dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the table and examples illustrating identification practice where each embodiment must be treated individually. When common rejection/objection applies to all embodiments, referencing the dependent claim number suffices. 35 U.S.C. 132 requires each Office action make explicit what rejection/objection applies to each claim embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee treatment for multiple dependent claims (use of PTO/SB/07)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in computation of fees for multiple dependent claims use a 'Multiple Dependent Claim Fee Calculation Sheet' (PTO/SB/07) with PTO/SB/06; OPAP places form in application file when multiple dependent claims are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple dependent claims are later added by amendment, TC technical support staff will place the form in the file. Calculate total independent and dependent claims for fee purposes on PTO/SB/07 then transfer to PTO/SB/06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of fees: proper vs improper multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Proper multiple dependent claim: a multiple dependent claim is considered to be that number of dependent claims to which it refers. (b) Improper multiple dependent claim: If none of the multiple dependent claims is proper, the fee will not be required. However, fee is required if at least one multiple dependent claim is proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any multiple dependent claim is improper, OPAP may mark it with an encircled '1' in the 'Dep. Claims' column of PTO/SB/07. An improper multiple dependent claim defective for non-alternative form or for depending on a prior multiple dependent claim will be counted as one dependent claim for fee calculation. Any claim depending from an improper multiple dependent claim is also considered improper and counted as one dependent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee calculation counting rules and example
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed example counting independent and dependent claims, including how proper multiple dependent claims count as multiple "Dep." numerals, how singular claims depending on multiple dependent claims inherit the count, and how improper claims are marked with an encircled '1'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the example to place numerals in 'Ind.' and 'Dep.' columns, add columns to get total independent and dependent claims, then place numbers on PTO/SB/06 to calculate fee. Example explains why certain claims are counted as '2' or encircled '1' for improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper dependent claims (37 CFR 1.75(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim which is in dependent form but which is so worded that it, in fact, is not [a proper dependent claim] will be required to be canceled as not being a proper dependent claim; and cancellation of any further claim depending on such a dependent claim will be similarly required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such claims should be objected to under 37 CFR 1.75(c) and require cancellation or rewriting in independent form. Ex parte Porter cited: treat as formal matter (object/cancel or replace) rather than rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, fourth paragraph. Applicant may amend to proper dependent form or redraft as independent upon payment of necessary fee. Note product-by-process exception and use form paragraph 7.36 for objections under 37 CFR 1.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper dependent claim test / Infringement test
rubrics_metrics.description: The test as to whether a claim is a proper dependent claim is that it shall include every limitation of the claim from which it depends (35 U.S.C. 112, fourth paragraph) or in other words that it shall not conceivably be infringed by anything which would not also infringe the basic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dependent claim does not lack compliance simply because there is a question as to the significance of the further limitation or whether it changes scope. Example: if claim 1 recites A,B,C,D, a claim reciting claim 1 with D omitted or replaced is not a proper dependent claim. Examiners are reminded that a dependent claim is directed to the combination of everything recited in base claim plus dependent limitations and must be compared with prior art as if it were an independent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim form and arrangement rules for dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of singular dependent claims is permissible in which a dependent claim refers to a preceding claim which, in turn, refers to another preceding claim. A claim which depends from a dependent claim should not be separated therefrom by any claim which does not also depend from said dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dependent claim may refer back to any preceding independent claim. Applicant's sequence should generally not be changed. During prosecution, numbering may change; numbering and references should be carefully checked when claims are renumbered upon allowance. Use form paragraph 7.43 to state objection when claim is dependent upon a rejected base claim but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis / Specification support for claim terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of every term used in any of the claims should be apparent from the descriptive portion of the specification with clear disclosure as to its import; in mechanical cases, it should be identified in the descriptive portion of the specification by reference to the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While applicant is not limited to nomenclature used in application as filed, appropriate amendment of the specification should be made when new terms are introduced to provide clear support or antecedent basis for new terms. Examiners should ensure terms used in claims presented late in prosecution find clear support/antecedent basis in the description so meaning may be ascertainable per 37 CFR 1.75(d)(1). If not, applicant required to amend description to provide support (without introducing new matter). Use form paragraph 7.44 to object: 'Claimed Subject Matter Not in Specification.' See MPEP § 2111.01 and § 2173.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of disclosure (enablement and utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure in an application, to be complete, must contain such description and details as to enable any person skilled in the art or science to which the invention pertains to make and use the invention as of its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential novelty must be described in sufficient detail including proportions and techniques where necessary. Specific operative embodiments or examples must be set forth; examples and description should be of sufficient scope to justify the scope of the claims. Markush claims require support for each member. Chemical compounds must be taught how to make. A complete disclosure should include a statement of utility. See MPEP § 2107, § 2107.01, § 2107.02, § 2107.03 and § 2164.06(a) for utility guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference rules (37 CFR 1.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference must be set forth in the specification and must (1) express a clear intent to incorporate by reference by using the root words 'incorporat(e)' and 'reference' and (2) clearly identify the referenced patent, application, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to conditions, inadvertently omitted portions present in prior-filed applications may be considered incorporated when certain priority/benefit claims are present, but the application must be amended to include the omitted portion within Office-set time (no later than close of prosecution). Applicant must supply a copy of the prior application, English translation if applicable, and identify where the omitted portion is found. 'Essential material' may be incorporated only by incorporation to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication (that does not itself incorporate the essential material) and is limited to material necessary for written description, claims, or means-plus-function structure (35 U.S.C. 112 requirements). Nonessential material may be incorporated by reference to various publications; incorporation by hyperlink or browser executable code is not permitted.
